extracted.intended_audience: Associated Press member editors, news bureaus, and war correspondents covering the Korean crisis and military reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and ground rules for news organizations (AP members) on handling and publishing military information during the Korean conflict, including voluntary censorship, embargoes, local publication of guard calls, and consultation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas guiding war news reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: War news reporting by the AP is being guided by two fundamental areas of responsibility: (A) military security, and (B) full, factual coverage of news not clearly subject to embargo for actual security reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters and editors must balance the need to protect military security with the obligation to provide full, factual coverage; disclosures (notably atomic matters) raise special issues and are to be treated with particular care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary censorship in fighting zones
rubrics_metrics.description: Censorship in the actual fighting zones in Korea, as well as in Japan and at other military bases, is on a voluntary basis, so far.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General MacArthur's command has set forth general guidance on security matters and asked correspondents to prevent North Koreans from learning 'strategic or helpful information.' Correspondents must follow the voluntary security guidance issued by military public relations officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of military-information restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Military information is, of course, subject to being (A) withheld by officers in the field, (B) embargoed at briefing sessions or by specific order, or (C) delayed until released by a headquarters spokesman or communique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporters should treat information flagged or handled in these three ways as restricted and refrain from publishing until the appropriate withholding/embargo/delay is lifted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for failing to adhere to ground rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondents failing to adhere to the specified or implied ground rules, under existing conditions, are subject to (A) denial of access to army communications between Korea and Tokyo or the mainland of the United States, or (B) the risk of having their military accreditations rescinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliance carries concrete sanctions (communication blackouts, loss of accreditation). News staff should therefore follow the security procedures carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on publishing operational details
rubrics_metrics.description: Orders have been issued restricting publication of movements, status of equipment, designations of units, division size, strength of units and advance sailing dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When these restrictions are properly recognized and executed by military public relations officers there has been little or no confusion — reporters should treat such operational details as off-limits unless expressly cleared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on publicity for National Guard/Reserve roundups
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army asked that there be no more state or national roundups of National Guard or Reserve units called to active duty; stories on calls to these units by state governors be published or broadcast only in the unit's own locality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A newspaper should publish only the name of the unit called that brings men in from its own circulation range; radio stations should follow the same locality rule. AP bureaus may carry announcements of national guard calls only if and when publicly and formally issued by governors or other appropriate authorities; individual outlets determine how to apply the Army's special request.

rubrics_metrics.name: AP responsibilities on embargoes and self-censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: The Associated Press recognizes its responsibilities are (A) to be guided by the appropriately stated and specified security embargoes and (B) not to indulge in self-censorship where no appropriate or authoritative restrictions are imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In all cases of doubt bureaus have been asked to consult the New York general desk or the Washington bureau before withholding or publishing material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary censorship code for atomic matters
rubrics_metrics.description: A censorship code, similar to that covering voluntary censorship in World War II, has been authorized or issued by governmental authorities for disclosures of atomic matters, though responsibilities are not yet fully or clearly defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Atomic-related disclosures require heightened caution; reporters should treat such material under the new voluntary code and seek guidance when the scope of restrictions is unclear.
